description: Verify that post-BOUND DUT emits an ARP Probe (sender_ip=0, target_ip=offered yiaddr) to verify the offered address is not in use (RFC 2131 §4.4.1)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 2131 §4.4.1 says the client SHOULD probe the assigned address with ARP before using it, in case another host is silently squatting. The Probe shape mirrors RFC 5227: sender_ip = 0, target_ip = offered yiaddr.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DORA: DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK → BOUND.
2. DUT → wire: ARP Probe
   • sender_proto_ip == 0
   • target_proto_ip == offered yiaddr   ← key check

[Pass condition]
ARP Probe with the expected sender/target IP shape lands within the deadline.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover / Fail_no_request — DORA broken before BOUND
• Fail_arp_probe_shape_mismatch — Probe has wrong sender/target fields
• Fail_no_arp_probe — DUT did not emit any ARP Probe after BOUND

verdicts.Pass: Post-BOUND ARP Probe has correct shape — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_arp_probe: No DUT ARP Probe after BOUND
